es: Mantener una sobremesa natural combinando ecos, cabeza y cola, elipsis y marcadores: proponer un tema, reaccionar con naturalidad y cambiar de tema o reconducirlo.

teaching.en: “Please help yourself to more,” said the host. “Did you like the recipe? My grandmother would be thrilled to hear it.”
teaching.es: «Por favor, sírvete más», dijo el anfitrión. «¿Te gustó la receta? A mi abuela le encantaría saberlo.»
teaching.explanationEs: Help yourself invita a servirse sin ceremonias; la receta abre un tema fácil para la sobremesa.

teaching.en: “I bet the boys will polish off that dessert before we reach the coffee.” “They will, won't they? They always do.”

teaching.explanationEs: Polish off significa terminar algo con rapidez; la tag won't they? pide compartir la opinión.

teaching.en: “Have you heard the gossip about the neighbours?” “No. Go on, I'm all ears, and don't leave out the best part.”
teaching.es: «¿Has oído el chisme sobre los vecinos?» «No. Sigue, soy todo oídos, y no te dejes la mejor parte.»
teaching.explanationEs: Go on invita al otro a seguir; combina bien con un eco o con una petición de detalles.

teaching.explanationEs: Neither can I copia el auxiliar de can't; do the dishes es la colocación para lavar los platos.

teaching.en: A running joke about the burnt toast, repeated every Christmas, is one way the host can steer the conversation back to lighter ground.
teaching.es: Una broma recurrente sobre la tostada quemada, repetida cada Navidad, es una forma en que el anfitrión puede reconducir la conversación hacia temas más ligeros.
teaching.explanationEs: Steer the conversation describe cambiar el rumbo con suavidad, por ejemplo con un chiste o un marcador.

teaching.en: After the main course, Tom stood up to propose a toast to the host, and everybody laughed at his long introduction.
teaching.es: Después del plato principal, Tom se puso de pie para proponer un brindis por el anfitrión, y todos se rieron de su larga introducción.
teaching.explanationEs: Propose a toast es la colocación habitual; el brindis suele cerrar la sobremesa con humor.

prompt.es: ¿Qué eco de Carlos muestra interés por lo que cuenta Sara?

choices.text: Does she? Lucky you, then.
Did she? Lucky you, then.
Is she? Lucky you, then.
Has she? Lucky you, then.

feedback.es: La frase principal usa gave (pasado simple), así que el eco repite did con el pronombre she; los otros auxiliares no corresponden.

hint.es: Repite el auxiliar que corresponde al verbo gave.

origin.text: Sara put the soup on the table. “My grandmother, she gave me the recipe,” she said, “on my birthday.” Carlos wanted to show interest in the story.

feedback.es: Go on invita a continuar con un chisme o una historia; come on también sirve para animar, pero go on es la ficha que mantiene viva la charla.

hint.es: Dos palabras: el verbo de movimiento + on.

origin.text: “By the way, have you heard the gossip about Mia?” “No. ___ on, tell me! I want to know everything.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Yo tampoco, y no podría comer ni un bocado más.»

answer.text: Neither can I, and I couldn't eat another bite

feedback.es: Neither can I copia can't de la frase anterior; la segunda parte añade la razón con couldn't y another bite.

hint.es: Empieza con la elipsis negativa y añade la razón después de la coma.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué insinúa Sara al final.

choices.text: That the soup was better than the dessert.
That Tom's toast had been too long.
That the guests should help with the dishes.
That she would rather do them alone.

feedback.es: Sara elogia sin decirlo de forma directa: «Neither of you has offered to do the dishes» es una indirecta para que los invitados ayuden.

origin.audio: Tom stood up and tapped his glass. “A toast to our host,” he said. “The soup, it was brilliant.” “Hear, hear,” said Carlos. “And the dessert, it was even better.” Sara laughed. “Neither of you has offered to do the dishes, though.” “Go on, Tom,” said Carlos. “You proposed the toast, so you can start the washing-up.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Mia intentó reconducir la conversación hacia las vacaciones.»

feedback.es: Steer the conversation es la colocación más natural para cambiar el rumbo con suavidad; guide y direct también funcionan.

origin.text: Mia noticed that the talk had turned to money, so she tried to ___ the conversation towards holidays before anyone got upset.

prompt.es: Escribe una sobremesa de unas 170 palabras con los cuatro recursos.

answer.text:
Tom: By the way, have you heard the gossip about Mia? She's moving to Madrid.
Sara: No way! Is she? Since when?
Tom: Since last week. Her company, it offered her a great job there.
Carlos: Did it? Good for her. To be honest, she always wanted to live abroad.
Sara: She's very brave, Mia, isn't she?
Tom: Very. I'd miss her, though. She's a lovely friend.
Carlos: So would I. Anyway, this soup, it's delicious. Did you make it, Sara?
Sara: I did. My grandmother, she gave me the recipe.
Carlos: Did she? Lucky you. Mind you, I couldn't eat another bite, and I'd love to try the dessert.
Sara: Go on, then. Help yourself. Shall we do the dishes afterwards?
Carlos: I'd love that. Thank you both.
Sara: And Tom still has to propose a toast.
Tom: So I do! Cheers, everyone. To Mia, and to her new job!

feedback.es: Una buena sobremesa propone un tema con marcador, reacciona con ecos o elipsis, usa cabeza o cola y cambia de tema con otro marcador.

origin.text: Situación: sobremesa en casa de Sara con Carlos y Tom. Tom propone un tema con una noticia (Mia se muda a Madrid). Escribe el intercambio (Sara/Carlos/Tom) de unas 170 palabras con: el tema propuesto con un marcador, dos reacciones (un eco y una elipsis), una cabeza o una cola y un cambio de tema con un marcador.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué pregunta Sara por el postre.

choices.text: To hint that the meal should finish soon.
To check that Carlos had not eaten everything.
To tease Tom about his strong opinions.
To move the talk away from a subject causing tension.

feedback.es: Sara lo pregunta con naturalidad justo después de la discusión por el dinero, y Tom «realised what she was doing»: es una maniobra para alejar la charla de la tensión, no una pregunta sobre el postre.

origin.audio: The dinner had been going well until Tom began to argue about money again. Mia had stopped eating, and nobody was looking at anyone else. Sara, who was the host, caught Mia's eye. “Has anyone tried the dessert yet?” she asked brightly. “I have,” said Carlos, “and I'll polish off whatever is left.” Everybody laughed, including Tom, who realised what she was doing. “Fair enough,” he said. “I'll stop. Mind you, I was right.” That has become a running joke at their table: Tom is always right, and always told to stop.

feedback.es: Help yourself es la invitación fija a servirse; ningún otro verbo forma esa expresión.

origin.text: The host moved the dish towards me and said, “Please ___ yourself; there is lots more in the kitchen.”

answer.text: He's a great cook, your brother, isn't he
accepted: He's a great cook, your brother, isn't he
Your brother, he's a great cook, isn't he

feedback.es: La cola nombra a tu hermano al final y la tag isn't he? concuerda con he; también funciona con la cabeza delante.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere el texto sobre la reacción de los invitados?

choices.text: That their reaction was cooler than Carlos had hoped.
That they doubted that his sister had really been offered it.
That they were upset by his sister's good luck.
That Carlos had not explained the news clearly.

feedback.es: Un eco sin pregunta de seguimiento y el silencio posterior indican interés escaso; Sara lo nota y cambia de tema por cortesía. El texto no habla de envidia ni de dudas.

origin.text: After the meal, Carlos told the table that his sister had been offered a job abroad. “Has she?” said Mia. “That's something.” Nobody asked where, or what the job was. Sara looked at Carlos, who was staring at his plate, and quickly offered more coffee. Mia asked for more bread, and the talk moved on to the weather.

prompt.es: Escucha y deduce qué piensa realmente el hablante de la comida.

choices.text: It was good enough that the speaker ate three plates willingly.
It was poor, but the speaker kept quiet out of kindness.
It was poor, and the speaker said so openly to his brother.
It was ordinary, and the speaker was simply very hungry.

feedback.es: El hablante dice que su hermano cocina fatal y confiesa que comió tres platos por educación y sin decir palabra: no le gustó y lo disimuló.

origin.audio: “My brother, he's a terrible cook. Burns everything, that man.” “Is he? I thought he made the pasta.” “He did, and I ate three plates of it out of kindness. Honestly, I don't know how I finished them, and I certainly didn't say a word.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Cada Navidad cuenta la misma historia y ya es una broma recurrente.»

feedback.es: A running joke es la colocación para una broma que se repite con el tiempo; running gag también existe, pero es más propia del teatro y la televisión.

origin.text: Every Christmas my uncle tells the same story about the burnt chicken, and it has become a running ___ in our family.
